https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research.who: Paul Hudak, John Hughes, Simon Peyton Jones and Philip Wadler, Haskell designers
https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research.where: A History of Haskell: Being Lazy with Class, HOPL III, section 12.3
https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research.says: Names Darcs and Pugs as the open-source projects that began attracting people to Haskell, tells how Tang chose Perl 6 after reading TAPL, and says Pugs had about 200 contributors within a year.

https://andrewshitov.com/2015/05/05/inte.who: Audrey Tang, Pugs creator, interviewed by Andrew Shitov
https://andrewshitov.com/2015/05/05/inte.says: Says Pugs chiefly drew newcomers to Haskell, some of whom, including Edward Kmett, went on to energise its community, and that Pugs's feedback helped firm up several GHC extensions.

https://www.lua.org/doc/jucs05.pdf.who: Roberto Ierusalimschy, Luiz Henrique de Figueiredo and Waldemar Celes, Lua's authors
https://www.lua.org/doc/jucs05.pdf.says: Cites Perl 6's planned register-based Parrot VM as a sign of growing interest in register machines, while claiming Lua 5.0 as the first widely used register-based VM.

https://mural.maynoothuniversity.ie/1018.who: Yunhe Shi, Kevin Casey, M. Anton Ertl and David Gregg, VM researchers
https://mural.maynoothuniversity.ie/1018.where: Virtual Machine Showdown: Stack Versus Registers, ACM TACO 4(4)
https://mural.maynoothuniversity.ie/1018.says: Says the stack-versus-register debate resurfaced because Parrot, the intermediate representation for Perl 6, was designed as a register machine rather than a stack machine.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parrot_vir.says: Says none of the languages hosted on Parrot made it their primary implementation, and that active development was declared over in August 2021, with MoarVM having taken over for Perl 6.

https://mail.python.org/archives/list/py.says: Says the Python 3000 work should be less sweeping than the Perl 6 redesign.

https://www.artima.com/weblogs/viewpost..where: Artima weblog, Python 3000 – Adaptation or Generic Functions?
https://www.artima.com/weblogs/viewpost..says: Describing the Python 3000 process, says with a smiley that its aim is to keep Perl 6 from happening again.

https://www.linuxjournal.com/magazine/in.who: Guido van Rossum, interviewed by James Gray
https://www.linuxjournal.com/magazine/in.says: Answers a suggestion that Python 3 is unusual in breaking compatibility by pointing to Perl 6, which he calls an entirely new language with a wholly different implementation.

https://mail.python.org/pipermail/python.where: python-3000 mailing list, Type Expressions thread
https://mail.python.org/pipermail/python.says: Dismisses proposed bracket notations for parameter lists, reminding the list that Python does not want to imitate Perl 6.
Replying to a call for Unicode characters used purely for fun, in the PEP 3131 identifiers debate, warns that this path ends in Perl 6 and Python must stay a sane alternative.

https://mail.python.org/archives/list/py.says: Argues that a language cannot be designed by committee, since every proposal put to a vote would fail, and says the Perl 6 and Tcl teams should learn from that.

https://mail.python.org/archives/list/py.where: python-dev, PEP 4000 thread on ruling out another Py3k-style break
https://mail.python.org/archives/list/py.says: Jokes that if anyone ever designs a new language and calls it Python 4, they should be stopped from repeating what happened with Perl 6.

https://peps.python.org/pep-3117/.says: An April Fools' proposal for Unicode type markers, it claims this would bring Python level with Perl 6's Unicode operators, then footnotes that it would if Perl 6 existed.

https://esdiscuss.org/topic/complexity-t.says: Assures the list that nobody on the ES4 effort intends the language to resemble Perl 6.

https://esdiscuss.org/topic/thread-about.where: es-discuss, Thread about ES6 on reddit
https://esdiscuss.org/topic/thread-about.says: Likens the situation to Perl 6 versus Perl 5, calling Perl 6 rich in good ideas that could only arrive by breaking compatibility.

https://github.com/golang/proposal/blob/.who: Ian Lance Taylor, Go core team
https://github.com/golang/proposal/blob/.says: Its Perl section traces Perl 6 from a 2000 start to a 2015 specification, calls it deliberately incompatible and ever-changing, and lists not being Perl 6 among Go's lessons, with keeping deadlines and gradual change.

https://go.dev/doc/go1.12.says: Says the go directive in a go.mod file now records which language version the module's files are written in.

https://go.dev/blog/compat.where: Go blog, Backward Compatibility, Go 1.21, and Go 2
https://go.dev/blog/compat.says: States that no Go 2 will ever break existing Go 1 programs.

https://forums.swift.org/t/design-priori.where: Swift Forums, Design priorities for the Swift 6 language mode, post 57
https://forums.swift.org/t/design-priori.says: Cites the Perl 5 to 6 move, which never took place, beside Swift 2 to 3 and Python 2 to 3 as lessons for planning Swift 6's language mode.

https://contributors.scala-lang.org/t/mo.where: Scala Contributors forum, Move slowly and iterate, post 23
https://contributors.scala-lang.org/t/mo.says: Contrasts Perl 6, which he says stayed announced but unreleased for ages, with Scala 3, due to reach feature freeze that summer.

https://users.rust-lang.org/t/twir-quote.where: Rust users forum, TWiR quote of the week thread, post 187
https://users.rust-lang.org/t/twir-quote.says: Puts forward as quote of the week Klabnik's remark that he does not want a situation like Ruby 1.9's, Python 3's or Perl 6's.

https://forum.dlang.org/post/me239u$1uj0.where: D newsgroup, thread on choosing between Go and D
https://forum.dlang.org/post/me239u$1uj0.says: Saying the D1 to D2 change nearly destroyed D, asks whether Perl 6 had not suffered a similar convulsion, and with less success than Python 3.

https://externals.io/message/76753#76755.says: Warns that PHP 7 could become the Perl 6 of the decade, an example of what happens when a project discards everything at once.

https://externals.io/message/92960#92968.says: Objects to the 2016 pipe operator RFC that it pushes PHP syntax too far in the Perl 6 direction.

https://wiki.php.net/rfc/pipe-operator-v.says: Proposes the |> pipe operator for PHP; the RFC passed its vote and is marked implemented for PHP 8.5.

https://wiki.php.net/rfc/php6.who: Andrea Faulds and Zeev Suraski, RFC authors
https://wiki.php.net/rfc/php6.where: PHP RFC: Name of Next Release of PHP
https://wiki.php.net/rfc/php6.says: Among its reasons for skipping version 6, notes that both the abandoned PHP 6 and Perl 6 had failed; the vote chose PHP 7 by 58 to 24.

https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/8.says: Suggests keeping a list of features that later Rust-inspired languages should adopt, describing such a language as a Rust 2.0 spared the turmoil of Perl 6 or Python 3.

https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/2.where: rust-lang/rfcs PR #2052, Evolving Rust through Epochs
https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/2.says: Notes that the Perl 6 community separates the language, Perl 6, from its canonical implementation, Rakudo, and proposes versioning Rust's language and toolchain separately.

https://github.com/Perl/PPCs/blob/main/d.says: Lists the Perl 6 RFC round, whose proposals nobody could see a way to build, among the failures the new proposal process should avoid, linking a critique of it.

https://rust-lang.github.io/rfcs/0002-rf.says: Setting up Rust's RFC process, suggests drawing on Python's PEP process if a stricter procedure becomes necessary.

https://www.cs.tufts.edu/~nr/cs257/archi.who: Allen Wirfs-Brock and Brendan Eich, ES2015 editor and JavaScript's creator
https://www.cs.tufts.edu/~nr/cs257/archi.where: JavaScript: The First 20 Years, HOPL IV
https://www.cs.tufts.edu/~nr/cs257/archi.says: Credits Perl for JavaScript's regular expressions and several array and string methods, and Python for generators, destructuring and comprehensions; Perl 6 is never mentioned.

https://nondot.org/sabre/.says: Names Swift's influences as including Haskell, Rust, Objective-C, Python, Ruby, CLU and C#, plus many unnamed others; Perl is absent.

https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q2052676.says: Raku's item lists ten languages it was influenced by, Python and Haskell among them, while no language item names Raku as an influence.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raku_(prog.says: Its infobox lists Perl, Haskell and AntLang as languages Raku influenced, citing Audrey Tang's 2010 post for the first two; the body makes no such claim.

https://web.archive.org/web/201004250029.where: How to Implement Perl 6 in '10, PerlMonks reply reposted on her blog
https://web.archive.org/web/201004250029.says: Recounts that Pugs work led to Moose and other CPAN releases for Perl 5, and that Pugs needed Haskell features later adopted in Haskell 2010 or implemented in GHC.

https://downloads.haskell.org/~ghc/old_d.says: Documents pattern guards as a GHC language extension, presenting them as a shortened form of a proposal by Simon Peyton Jones.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haskell.says: Its infobox counts Raku among the languages Haskell influenced, footnoting a glossary page on a Perl 6 wiki; the article text mentions Pugs only in a list of Haskell applications.

https://docs.raku.org/language/faq.says: Describes Raku as a sibling of Perl and makes no claim that Raku influenced any language beyond the Perl family.

https://github.com/trizen/sidef.says: Presents Sidef as a language drawing on Ruby and Raku, plus built-in computer algebra and exact rationals by default.

https://developers.slashdot.org/story/16.who: Larry Wall, interviewed by Slashdot readers
https://developers.slashdot.org/story/16.where: The Slashdot Interview With Larry Wall
https://developers.slashdot.org/story/16.says: Says other languages took Perl 5's regexes, jokes that a PHP borrowing enough to be consistent would have reimplemented Perl 6, and credits C#, Erlang, Go and Haskell for Perl 6's concurrency ideas.

https://perl.org.il/presentations/larry-.where: Present Continuous, Future Perfect, OSDC::Israel talk transcript
https://perl.org.il/presentations/larry-.says: Observes that everyone borrowed Perl 5's regexes and predicts that people will abandon PCRE in favour of Perl 6 regexes.
